title: Great cities and places
summary: A short tour of four famous places: Cairo and the pyramids of Giza beside the Nile, Petra in Jordan, the old medina of Fez in Morocco, and Dubai, old and new. On the way you practise comparing places with أَكْبَرُ مِنْ (bigger than), naming the very best with أَقْدَمُ (the oldest), and saying where you want to go: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَزُورَ (I would like to visit).

hero.alt: The pyramids of Giza in the desert under a blue sky, with three small pyramids in front
hero.caption: The pyramids of Giza. The nearest large pyramid is Menkaure's; behind it stand Khafre's and the Great Pyramid of Khufu.

sections.title: Cairo, the Nile and the pyramids
body: Cairo, الْقَاهِرَة, is the capital of Egypt, مِصْر, and one of the biggest cities in Africa and the Arab world. It lies on both banks of the Nile, النِّيل, one of the longest rivers on earth. For thousands of years most Egyptians have lived close to the river, because most of the rest of the country is desert. Historic Cairo, with its old mosques, markets and city gates, has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1979.

On the edge of the city, at Giza, الْجِيزَة, stand the pyramids, الْأَهْرَام; one pyramid is a هَرَم. The Great Pyramid was built for the king Khufu about 4,500 years ago. It is the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World and the only one still standing. Near it lies the Sphinx, which Arabic calls أَبُو الْهَوْل ('father of terror'). The pyramids belong to the World Heritage site 'Memphis and its Necropolis', also listed in 1979.

sentences.en: The pyramids are much older than Petra.
sentences.literal: the pyramids (are) older than Petra by much

sentences.ar: النِّيل مِنْ أَطْوَلِ الْأَنْهَار فِي الْعَالَم.
sentences.en: The Nile is one of the longest rivers in the world.
sentences.literal: the Nile (is) of the longest (of) the rivers in the world

sentences.en: I visited Cairo and saw the pyramids of Giza.
sentences.literal: I visited Cairo and I saw (the) pyramids (of) Giza

sentences.en: Cairo is the biggest city in Egypt.
sentences.literal: Cairo (is the) biggest (of a) city in Egypt

mistakes.why: After the superlative a singular noun has no al-: akbaru madīna.

sections.title: Petra, city of the Nabataeans

photo.alt: The carved stone front of the Treasury at Petra, with columns and statues, cut into pink-red rock
photo.caption: الْخَزْنَة, 'the Treasury', carved into the rock face at Petra.

body: Petra, الْبَتْرَاء, in the south of Jordan, الْأُرْدُنّ, was the capital of the Nabataeans, الْأَنْبَاط, an Arab people who grew rich from the caravan trade in incense and spices more than 2,000 years ago. They carved tombs, temples and houses straight into the red and pink sandstone, which is why Petra is often called the 'rose-red city'. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1985.

Most visitors walk in through the Siq, السِّيق, a narrow gorge more than a kilometre long. At its end the most famous monument suddenly appears: الْخَزْنَة, 'the Treasury', carved about 2,000 years ago. The name comes from an old story that treasure was hidden in the stone urn at the top; in fact it was probably the tomb of a Nabataean king. The verb يَنْحِتُ (he carves) describes exactly how Petra was made.

sentences.en: The Treasury is the most famous place in Petra.
sentences.literal: the Treasury (is the) most famous place in Petra

sentences.en: The Nabataeans carved the Treasury into the rock.
sentences.literal: carved the Nabataeans the Treasury in the rock

sentences.ar: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَزُورَ الْبَتْرَاء فِي الرَّبِيع.
sentences.en: I would like to visit Petra in spring.
sentences.literal: I want that I visit Petra in the spring

sections.title: The old medina of Fez

photo.alt: The Chouara tannery in Fez: many round stone vats of coloured dye between old yellow houses
photo.caption: The Chouara دَبَّاغَة (tannery) in the old medina of Fez, where leather has been dyed by hand for centuries.

body: Fez, فَاس, in the north of Morocco, was founded at the end of the 8th century, which makes it older than Marrakesh, مَرَّاكُش. Its old town, Fes el-Bali, is one of the largest historic medinas in the world and has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1981. In Arabic it is simply الْمَدِينَة الْقَدِيمَة (the old city). Many of its lanes are so narrow, ضَيِّق, that cars cannot enter, and goods are still carried by donkeys and handcarts.

In the medina stands the Qarawiyyin, الْقَرَوِيِّين, a mosque and place of learning founded in 859 by a woman, Fatima al-Fihri. It is often described as the oldest university in the world that is still working. Not far away is the Chouara tannery, a دَبَّاغَة, where workers dye leather by hand in stone vats, as in the photo. The bags, slippers and jackets made from it are sold in the nearby سُوق (market).

mistakes.why: 'Than' is always مِنْ after a comparative.

sentences.en: The streets of the old city are very narrow.
sentences.literal: (the) streets (of) the city the old (are) narrow very

mistakes.why: The plural of a thing counts as 'she', so the adjective is feminine: ḍayyiqa.

sentences.ar: اِشْتَرَيْتُ حَقِيبَةً مِنَ الْجِلْد فِي سُوقِ فَاس.
sentences.en: I bought a leather bag in the market of Fez.
sentences.literal: I bought a bag of the leather in (the) market (of) Fez

sections.title: Dubai, old and new

photo.alt: A small wooden water taxi crossing Dubai Creek, with buildings along the water and towers in the distance
photo.caption: An عَبْرَة, a small water taxi, crossing خَوْرُ دُبَيّ (Dubai Creek).

body: Dubai, دُبَيّ, is one of the seven emirates of the United Arab Emirates; the capital of the country is Abu Dhabi. Old Dubai grew up around the Creek, خَوْرُ دُبَيّ, a long arm of the sea where pearl divers, fishermen and traders once kept their wooden boats. People still cross the Creek today in an عَبْرَة, a small water taxi, and the old markets for spices and gold lie close to its banks.

In the old Al Fahidi quarter many houses have wind towers, بَرَاجِيل, which caught the breeze and cooled the rooms long before air conditioning. A short ride away stands the new Dubai of glass and steel. Its best-known building is the Burj Khalifa, بُرْجُ خَلِيفَة, opened in 2010 and about 828 metres high. Here a superlative is the natural thing to say: أَطْوَلُ بُرْج فِي الْعَالَم (the tallest tower in the world).

sentences.ar: بُرْجُ خَلِيفَة أَطْوَلُ بُرْجٍ فِي الْعَالَم.
sentences.en: The Burj Khalifa is the tallest tower in the world.
sentences.literal: (the) tower (of) Khalifa (is the) tallest tower in the world
segs: Khalifa ('Burj Khalifa', the tower in Dubai)

sentences.en: We took an abra on Dubai Creek.
sentences.literal: we rode an abra in (the) creek (of) Dubai

sentences.ar: فِي رَأْيِي، دُبَيّ الْقَدِيمَة أَجْمَلُ مِنْ دُبَيّ الْجَدِيدَة.
sentences.en: In my opinion, old Dubai is more beautiful than new Dubai.
sentences.literal: in my opinion, Dubai the old (is) more beautiful than Dubai the new

words.note: Plural أَهْرَام; the pyramids of Giza are الْأَهْرَام.

words.en: the Siq (the narrow gorge into Petra)

words.note: Many people in the Gulf say it with a long ō: khōr.
A Gulf word that came from Persian; the singular is bārjīl.

reading.title: My journeys
reading.ar: زُرْتُ الْقَاهِرَة فِي السَّنَةِ الْمَاضِيَة. شَاهَدْتُ الْأَهْرَام وَأَبَا الْهَوْل، وَرَكِبْتُ مَرْكَبًا فِي النِّيل. الْأَهْرَام أَقْدَمُ مَكَان زُرْتُهُ فِي حَيَاتِي. بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ سَافَرْتُ إِلَى الْأُرْدُنّ وَمَشَيْتُ فِي السِّيق إِلَى الْخَزْنَة. كَانَتِ الصُّخُورُ وَرْدِيَّةً وَجَمِيلَةً جِدًّا. فِي السَّنَةِ الْقَادِمَة أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَزُورَ فَاس، لِأَنَّ مَدِينَتَهَا الْقَدِيمَة مِنْ أَجْمَلِ الْمُدُن فِي الْعَالَم. حُلْمِي أَيْضًا أَنْ أَرَى دُبَيّ مِنْ بُرْجِ خَلِيفَة.
reading.en: Last year I visited Cairo. I saw the pyramids and the Sphinx, and I took a boat on the Nile. The pyramids are the oldest place I have visited in my life. After that I travelled to Jordan and walked through the Siq to the Treasury. The rocks were pink and very beautiful. Next year I would like to visit Fez, because its old city is one of the most beautiful cities in the world. My dream is also to see Dubai from the Burj Khalifa.
segs: and I rode, and I took (a boat)
Khalifa ('Burj Khalifa', the tower in Dubai)

readingQuestions.prompt: What did the writer do on the Nile?
readingQuestions.explain: رَكِبْتُ مَرْكَبًا فِي النِّيل: I took a boat on the Nile.

readingQuestions.prompt: What does the writer say about the pyramids?
options: They are the oldest place the writer has visited.
They are the tallest building in the world.
readingQuestions.explain: الْأَهْرَام أَقْدَمُ مَكَان زُرْتُهُ: the pyramids are the oldest place I have visited.

readingQuestions.prompt: Which city does the writer want to visit next year?
readingQuestions.explain: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَزُورَ فَاس: I would like to visit Fez.

quiz.prompt: Which people carved Petra into the rock?
quiz.explain: Petra was the capital of the Nabataeans, an Arab people who grew rich from the incense trade.

options: I would like to visit Petra.
quiz.explain: أُرِيدُ أَنْ + a verb ending in -a: I want to / I would like to.

quiz.prompt: Which is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing?
quiz.explain: The Great Pyramid, built about 4,500 years ago, is the oldest of the Seven Wonders and the only one left.

quiz.prompt: Which word fills the gap? الْأَهْرَام ___ مِنَ الْبَتْرَاء (The pyramids are older than Petra.)
quiz.explain: 'Older than' is أَقْدَمُ مِنْ; the comparative does not change for a plural.

quiz.prompt: What is الْمَدِينَة الْقَدِيمَة in Fez?
options: the old town (medina), a UNESCO World Heritage site
quiz.explain: The old medina of Fez has been a World Heritage site since 1981; many of its lanes are too narrow for cars.

quiz.prompt: What is an عَبْرَة in Dubai?
options: a small water taxi on the Creek
quiz.explain: People cross Dubai Creek in an abra, a small wooden water taxi.
